name: Southern Woodcraft, LLC
old_description: Handmade hardwood cabinets, vanities, wine rooms, closets, and more.
about:
Southern Woodcraft, LLC operates from Bluffton, South Carolina, where it produces custom hardwood cabinetry and millwork for residential clients. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

The shop specializes in handmade hardwood cabinets, vanities, wine rooms, and closets, along with custom furniture and built-ins. Its finish carpentry division handles trim work, stair railings, wainscoting, and custom millwork. All pieces are built to order using solid hardwood rather than particle board, and the company emphasizes a personalized design process from consultation through installation.

Southern Woodcraft serves homeowners in the Bluffton area and surrounding Lowcountry region, providing tailored solutions for kitchen and bath remodels, custom storage, and architectural woodwork. The company works directly with clients rather than through contractors, offering free quotes and collaborative design.

The business was founded on a reaction against mass-produced, low-quality cabinetry; its stated mission is to deliver lasting craftsmanship and materials that outperform typical particle-board construction. By focusing on one-on-one client relationships, the firm aims to align each project with the homeowner's style, budget, and timeline.

name: Southwest Prototyping
old_description: Coatings such as powder coating, anodizing, alodine and paint
about:
Southwest Prototyping operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, providing engineering and fabrication services to industrial and research clients. The company maintains a CAGE code (6FB48) for government contracting, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The shop combines mechanical, electrical, and software engineering with in-house fabrication. Capabilities span machine building and automation, systems integration, control systems, data acquisition, and test system development. The facility handles manual and CNC machining, welding, sheet metal work, plastics vacuforming, and casting of both plastics and metals. Finishing services include powder coating, anodizing, alodine treatment, and painting. On the electronics side, the team designs, assembles, and tests printed circuit boards, develops firmware for microcontrollers (Atmel, SiLabs, Microchip, ARM), and writes application software for Windows, Linux, and real-time platforms such as National Instruments LabVIEW.

Customers come from sectors aligned with the company's NAICS codes: industrial machinery manufacturing, electronic instrument production, control systems, engineering services, software development, research and design, and equipment repair. Typical engagements include rapid prototyping, design for manufacturability, reverse engineering, sensor integration, ruggedized electronics packaging, and alteration of commercial off-the-shelf products.

The breadth of disciplines under one roof—mechanical design, electronics, software, and finishing—allows Southwest Prototyping to take projects from concept through validated prototype without outsourcing critical steps.

name: Southwestern Medical Reps., Inc
old_description: is an independent distributor for multiple medical equipment manufacturers and suppliers.
about:
Southwestern Medical Reps, Inc. operates from Dallas, Texas, as an independent distributor and sales representative for medical equipment manufacturers. The company has served the healthcare rehabilitation market for over 30 years, representing multiple manufacturers across a seven-state region that includes Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, and Arizona. Leadership is headed by CEO Cara Colgin Smith, who directs a team of territory managers covering distinct geographic zones.

The firm does not manufacture products but provides a suite of field services that support the specification and adoption of rehabilitation technology. Its representatives supply free trial demonstration equipment for therapist and dealer evaluations, conduct in-service training on new rehab devices, and furnish current ordering information, clinical-study data, and sample medical-justification documentation. They also customize equipment configurations for individual patients and consult with rehabilitation clinics on cost-effective product selection. The team comprises seven specialists, each holding credentials such as ATP, PT, or COTA/L, who work directly with dealers, physical therapists, and occupational therapists.

Primary customers are rehabilitation facilities, clinics, dealers, and therapy professionals who require high-end mobility and positioning solutions. The company focuses on high-end rehabilitation manufacturers and distributors, bringing customized mobility solutions to providers, therapists, and facilities. Examples include physical therapists, occupational therapists, and rehab clinics across the Southwest.

The company distinguishes itself by acting as a consultant to rehabilitation clinics to determine the most cost-effective products and supplies, and by educating the market on the latest rehab technology. Their goal is to ensure the most appropriate equipment reaches the end user.

name: Southwestern Wire
old_description: Some of the website features are unavailable unless JavaScript is enabled.
about:
Southwestern Wire is headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, and traces its origins to March 1992 when Max Moore and Steve Peters acquired the machinery and equipment of Acme Fence and Iron from the Bank of Oklahoma. The founders spent the first year rebuilding and modernizing the plant, installing a state‑of‑the‑art wire galvanizing line that enabled heavier zinc coatings up to 1.2 oz./sq. ft. and positioned the company to compete with larger domestic and foreign wire manufacturers.

The company manufactures a broad range of wire and fence products: galvanized and vinyl‑coated chain link fence fabric (including preslatted and security mini‑mesh up to 20 ft tall), fabricated panel products such as residential bent‑frame gates, dog kennels and temporary fence panels, agricultural wire (vineyard, trellis, high‑tensile and electric fence wire), industrial low‑ and high‑carbon wire (C1006–C1026 and 1027–1065), recycling wire (single‑loop bale ties in black annealed and galvanized finishes), and galvanized tension bars, truss rods, drop rods and gate rods. Southwestern Wire owns and operates three manufacturing facilities in the United States — Norman, OK; Birmingham, AL; and Sacramento, CA — with a major 30,000 sq. ft. expansion added in 1998.

Primary customers are expert distributors in each product category. The company serves the chain link fence industry, industrial wire users, recycling and baling operations, high‑carbon wire markets, agricultural sectors (vineyards, cattle grazing), and security/prison construction where its mini‑mesh products are specified.

Southwestern Wire emphasizes domestic production — "products melted and manufactured in the United States of America" — and points to its 1993 establishment of the only mass‑production galvanized tension bar facility in the U.S. as a key differentiator. The ability to apply Class 5 galvanizing (2 oz./sq. ft.) meeting ASTM A392 Class 2, along with ongoing investments in technology and employee development, underpins its "Made In The USA" positioning.

name: Space Age Electronics

about:
Space Age Electronics was founded in 1963 in Mt Holly, North Carolina. The company designs and manufactures code-compliant fire and life safety solutions tailored to system integrators, operating from ISO 9001 certified facilities in the United States. Over six decades, it has developed a brand family that includes the Infinity Series of modular components alongside integration accessories, surge protection, and building control.

Its product portfolio spans integration accessories, surge protection, building control systems, specialty detection, modular components, emergency two-way communication, construction safety equipment, and panels and prefabricated assemblies. All products are designed and manufactured in-house at the company's U.S. facilities, which hold ISO 9001 certification.

The primary customers are fire and life safety system integrators who specify and install code-compliant systems for commercial, industrial, and institutional buildings. The company's solutions address fire protection, building automation, and construction safety requirements.

Space Age Electronics highlights its six-decade track record of American-made fire protection and life safety solutions as a key differentiator, stating that it stands behind every product to give integrators confidence and efficiency on complex projects.

name: Specialty Food Process Technologies, LLC
old_description: Clean-In-Place systems ensure consistent and repeatable cleaning of process equipment.
about:
Specialty Food Process Technologies, LLC is a process engineering and consulting firm based in Madison, Wisconsin. The company focuses exclusively on food and beverage processing, drawing on an engineering team with a combined 100 years of hands-on experience in the design, construction, and commissioning of turnkey processing plants.

The firm provides a range of engineering services, from early conceptual designs to detailed engineering packages. Core capabilities include Clean-In-Place (CIP) system design, liquid processing systems for blending and dosing liquids, slurries, gases, and powders, and thermal processing systems with automated temperature control and energy recovery. The company also conducts feasibility studies for plant revamps, develops life-cycle roadmaps for existing facilities, and designs aseptic processing and process control systems. A warehouse on site supports spare parts packing and shipping.

Specialty Food Process Technologies serves a broad spectrum of food and beverage sectors. Its project experience spans fluid milk processing, plant oil extraction, grape and orange juice production, tomato processing, milk powder, carbonated beverages, extended shelf-life products, packaged salads, sauces, fried foods, meat processing (ground beef, sausage), baking mixes, prepared meals, baker's yeast, grain handling, infant formula, sugar syrups, powdered ingredients, flavors, pet food, water, coffee, tea, plant-based proteins, and utility systems such as clean steam, compressed air, cooling towers, and glycol chillers. A recent engagement included engineering services and processing equipment for three greenfield fruit and vegetable plants for Pacific Concentrates.

The company emphasizes its hands-on experience as a differentiator, using it to help clients evaluate existing equipment, optimize asset use through life-cycle roadmaps, and solve unique processing problems. It positions itself as a partner for new facility projects and for revamping aging plants.

name: Specialty Foods
old_description: We're a family-owned, family-operated food company located in the heart of Middle Tennessee.
about:
Specialty Foods is a family-owned and family-operated food manufacturer based in La Vergne, Tennessee, in the heart of Middle Tennessee. The company was founded in 2009 by Randall "Randy" Sanders, who identified a gap in the bread market for a top-quality product baked with fine ingredients that delivered a genuine homemade taste. Sanders was later joined by his two sons, Wesley and Will, and together they built the business around three distinct brand lines.

The company produces three product families: Ma's Kitchen, which began in 1985 with a sourdough bread recipe passed down for over a century and initially supplied to restaurant chains; Ginny's Homemade Waffles, made with an age-old recipe that includes imported pearl sugar; and Mama Turney's Homemade Pies. Specialty Foods serves both the food-service channel and the consumer marketplace, emphasizing the use of the freshest ingredients and consistent quality across every batch.

Its customers include restaurant chains, food-service distributors, and retail consumers seeking wholesale or direct purchase options. The company highlights its wholesale resources and food-service resources as part of its offering, targeting operators who value consistent, made-from-scratch baked goods.

Sanders started Specialty Foods to deliver the true look, feel, and taste of homemade baking at a commercial scale, and the company states that its commitment to quality and consistency—every bite, every time—sets it apart from competitors.

about:
Specialty Woodworking Inc. operates from Bedford Park, Illinois, and has been producing custom cabinetry and millwork for over two decades. The company was established as a cabinetry shop serving the Chicago area and has since expanded its reach across the Midwest and the contiguous United States.

The company designs, fabricates, assembles, and installs custom cabinetry for both residential and commercial projects. Its in-house capabilities cover the full project lifecycle, from initial design through final installation, including kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, laundry room cabinets, and commercial millwork for offices and retail spaces.

Specialty Woodworking serves residential homeowners and commercial contractors, with completed projects in multiple states. Residential work includes kitchens, bathrooms, and laundry rooms, while commercial projects encompass offices, retail environments, and other business spaces.

The firm emphasizes quality, personalized service, and attention to detail, highlighting efficient project delivery, meticulous planning, and precision execution as key differentiators. It stands behind its products with a commitment to craftsmanship.

name: Specialty Woodworks, Inc.
old_description: When a project calls for high-end architectural woodwork and custom fabrication, rely on Specialty Woodworks.
about:
Specialty Woodworks, Inc. is based in Lexington, South Carolina. The company began three decades ago as a small workshop providing basic woodworking services.

It now operates as an architectural woodworking and custom design firm, offering design, engineering, fabrication, and installation for millwork, doors, window casings, and historic restoration. The engineering team produces shop drawings from client designs or creates custom designs, integrating with CAD-to-production workflows and CNC precision cutting equipment. In-house capabilities include millwork fabrication, door and casing fabrication, and pre-construction services, allowing the firm to handle projects of any scope. The company's precision-oriented equipment enables drilling, carving, and cutting materials to exacting standards without sacrificing quality.

The firm serves architects, designers, and general contractors who need high-end architectural woodwork for commercial and historic buildings. Its portfolio includes restoration, upfit, and repurposing projects, where in-house fabrication enables matching exacting historic specifications. Businesses seeking to preserve historic structures rather than demolish them are a noted client base.

Specialty Woodworks differentiates itself through uncompromising quality and craftsmanship, with installations meeting AWI quality standards. The company highlights its unlimited capabilities, pre-construction support, and a culture of pride in workmanship as reasons clients rely on them for complex architectural challenges.
